normalized.governing_thought: Margin is falling because of promotions, shrink and e-commerce delivery, not wages; fixing those first gets Harlow to ~3% by FY2028
executive_summary: Operating margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0% in two years (FY2023–FY2025); operating income fell from $47.9M to $15.3M while sales grew 6%.
About 80% of the fall is gross margin (deeper promotions, more shrink) and e-commerce fulfilment. Store labor explains 13%: wages rose 9.4%, but 6% fewer hours per sales dollar offset most of it.
E-commerce loses ~$10M a year once third-party delivery and sales taken from our own stores are counted.

Replace the 8% across-the-board labor cut with six actions: cut loss-making promotions, restore fresh and receiving routines to cut shrink, reprice delivery, grow private label, exit the nine loss-making stores, and target labor savings where hours are heaviest.
Result: ~$39M operating income (2.8%) in FY2028 on cautious assumptions; $5.5M of named stretch levers take it to 3.1%. Management's draft plan reaches ~1.5%.
Start with promotions, delivery pricing and shrink: fast, low-capital, partly tested. They should lift FY2026 to ~$24–28M, above the $20M covenant.
Approve the plan in place of the draft labor-cut plan, and launch wave 1 now.
Approve in principle the exit of the three loss-making stores whose leases run beyond 2027 ($7.5M one-time); store-by-store cases come to the next board meeting.
Keep home delivery, but repriced, with delivered-order growth on hold until each order covers its cost.

slides.title: Five risks could knock the plan off course; each has an early warning sign and an agreed response

claims.claim: Cutting promotions loses traffic to ValuMart
evidence: 11 stores opened in our trade areas since 2023
Warning sign: weekly traffic and comparable sales in stores within three miles of a ValuMart (already −4.2% in FY2025)
Response: cut first outside ValuMart areas; where traffic falls, put part of the saving into private label and everyday prices

claims.claim: Fewer hours raise shrink or hurt service
evidence: Warning sign: shrink % by store; checkout waits; stock-outs
Response: protect fresh and receiving hours; pause cuts in any store whose shrink rises 0.2 pts

claims.claim: Delivery customers leave after repricing
evidence: Warning sign: e-commerce sales against the test's −2%; switching to click-and-collect
Response: adjust fee and threshold; the test showed most delivery customers switch rather than leave

claims.claim: Costs rise further: delivery contract (+3% proposed), minimum wage (+4% in 2027)
evidence: Warning sign: contract terms at renewal; wage settlements
Response: plan already absorbs the full wage rise; rebid delivery if the provider will not hold rates

claims.claim: E-commerce cannibalisation estimate rests on a survey
evidence: Warning sign: basket and store-visit data for online customers
Response: low exposure: e-commerce loses money unless over 70% of its sales are new

slides.title: Where the pack is thin, we chose cautious assumptions; these are the ones that matter most

claims.claim: Limits of the evidence
evidence: Shrink and labor: the quartile pattern is a correlation across stores, not proof that fewer hours cause shrink.
Cannibalisation: the 70% figure is what customers say in a survey (n = 2,300). The conclusion holds unless over 70% of online sales are new.
Fee test: 4 stores over 10 weeks; chain-wide response may differ.
Stores: only combined figures for the nine stores are available; the 6/3 split is pro rata.

claims.claim: Choices made
evidence: Promotions: the valuation assumes promotional sales move to regular price rather than disappear; we stop at 4 of the ~11 points of share in money-losing events.
No market growth in the FY2028 sales base; margin gains come only from the actions.
Full wage pass-through: the 2027 rise is applied to all store labor, though not every employee is on the minimum wage. Partial pass-through would be upside.
Vendor funding recovery (46% back towards 55%) is not counted.
Timing: if FY2026 is largely booked by the time of the meeting, the covenant view on page 12 should be replaced with the actual result before it goes to the lender.

normalized.recommendation: Approve the plan in place of the draft labor-cut plan, and launch wave 1 now (promotion reset, chain-wide delivery pricing and contract renegotiation, fresh and receiving routines); approve in principle the exit of the three loss-making stores whose leases run beyond 2027 ($7.5M one-time), with store-by-store cases at the next board meeting; keep home delivery, but repriced, with delivered-order growth on hold until each order covers its cost.

alternatives_considered.option: Management's draft plan: 8% across-the-board labor (hour) cut, e-commerce frozen, all 58 stores kept
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: reaches only ~1.5% margin by FY2028 because it leaves the largest causes of the decline untouched; range 2.0% if the wage rise is ignored, ~1.0% if shrink rises as after the last hour cuts; the cut could give back half its savings through shrink; the freeze alone would leave the ~$10M e-commerce loss in place.

alternatives_considered.option: Targeted labor cut: 8% fewer hours in the most labor-heavy half of stores only
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen in place of the across-the-board cut (+$6.8M, wave 2), protecting fresh and receiving tasks in the leanest stores.

alternatives_considered.option: Freezing e-commerce / keeping delivery as is
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: the freeze alone would leave the ~$10M loss in place; instead keep delivery but reprice it, hold delivered volume flat and steer to click-and-collect.

alternatives_considered.option: Tested delivery pricing ($7.99 fee, free above $100)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: roll out chain-wide now; ~$2.5M a year net, keeps 98% of e-commerce sales; test the next fee step later.

alternatives_considered.option: Store exits: six at lease expiry vs three with longer leases
alternatives_considered.treatment: Both pursued via different routes: six at lease expiry by CEO decision (renegotiate rent first, close only if four-wall EBITDA stays negative); three longer-lease exits approved in principle by board ($7.5M one-time, ~3.4-year payback).
Rejected: evidence measures sales, not profit; 38% of events lose money; cut promotional share 29% → 25%.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Based only on the board briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data).
The shrink pattern across labor quartiles is a correlation across stores, not proof of cause.
Cannibalisation: the 70% figure is what customers say in a survey (n = 2,300); the conclusion holds unless over 70% of online sales are new.
Fee test: 4 stores over 10 weeks; chain-wide response may differ.
Lost contribution assumes all lost e-commerce sales leave Harlow at 20% contribution (cautious).
Split between the 6 and 3 stores assumes losses and sales are spread evenly (pack gives only combined figures); the 6/3 split is pro rata.
Closure costs other than lease exits are not in the pack; one-time costs other than the $7.5M lease exits need a CFO estimate.
Exits land across FY2027–FY2028 as leases end, so the full run-rate may come only in FY2029.
Promotions valuation assumes promotional sales move to regular price rather than disappear; stops at 4 of the ~11 points of share in money-losing events.
No market growth in the FY2028 sales base; margin gains come only from the actions.
Full wage pass-through: 2027 +4% minimum-wage rise applied to all store labor; partial pass-through would be upside.
Vendor funding recovery (46% back towards 55%) is not counted.

FY2026 in-year estimates assume half the promotion reset, 9 months of delivery pricing, a 0.15-pt shrink reduction, half a year of targeted labor savings and +0.5 pt private label, with the underlying business holding at FY2025 levels.
Timing: if FY2026 is largely booked by the time of the meeting, the covenant view should be replaced with the actual result before it goes to the lender.
Stretch levers ($5.5M) are named, not yet banked; reaching 3.0% needs at least $3.4M of them.

Risks: traffic loss to ValuMart, shrink/service from fewer hours, delivery customers leaving after repricing, further cost rises (delivery contract +3%, minimum wage +4%), survey-based cannibalisation estimate.
